Balmazujvaros Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Böszörményi út 62, Hungary

Not demolished. Established in 1872, this cemetery includes an ohel holding the community's first rabbi, Nathaniel Hakohen Fried, and his wife Pesl; Fried's halachic writings were published as 'Pné Mevin' and he founded a yeshiva here in 1894 that drew 30 students. The Orthodox community itself was founded in 1845 by five families who had relocated from Tiszadob, and grew steadily to nearly 400 people by the 1940s. The cemetery closed in 1944 and was formally protected in the late 1990s, when its mortuary, fence, and some tombs were restored.
